newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-CHELSEA V MIDDLESBROUGH MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-CHELSEA V MIDDLESBROUGH MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Strengths and weaknesses of the Chelsea and Middlesbrough teams who meet in the English F.A. Cup Final at Wembley Stadium on Saturday (kickoff 1400gmt):

Playing style: Effectively a fluid 3-5-2 system, Chelsea manager Ruud Gullitt has a team that looks far more comfortable going forward than defending. The defence has looked suspect this season, especially in the air, and especially if Frenchman Frank Lebouef has been missing. However on their day,with Mark Hughes playing in a holding role behind Gianfranco Zola, Chelsea can be devastating going forward. Skipper Dennis Wise has a key role in creating the openings for Hughes and Zola to exploit.

Strengths: Lebouef has proved to be one of the best buys of the season and when he plays well, the defensive half of the team look anchored and secure. Zola has been outstanding all season with some excellent goals. His power with freekicks around the box also cause opponents big problems. Chelsea also have the ability to attack down the wings thanks to Romanian defender Dan Petrescu who loves going forward.
Weaknesses: Mentally Chelsea are suspect and have developed a dangerous tendency to play well as a team in the big matches only, and take their foot off the gas in more routine leage games.

Motivation: For a club that likes to project a glamorous image and one supported by many well known celebrities, Chelsea as a club cannot compete with London rivals Arsenal and Tottenham in terms of trophies won down the years. They have won the leag ue once (1955) the Cup once (1970), the League Cup once (1965) and the European Cup Winners Cup once (1971). The death in a helicopter crash of their 42-year-old multi-millionaire deputy chairman Matthew Harding in October has also been a big inspiration for Chelsea who want to honour his memory with a trophy.

Playing style: Any team that gets relegated in the same season as reaching two Cup finals must have an unusual, confusing playing style. Welcome to Middlesbrough. Individually the team is packed with some fine players -- especially Juninho, Emerson, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Gianluca Festa and Nigel Pearson, but the team, which usually plays with a 4-1-3-2 formation only gels in fits and starts.

Strengths: Ravanelli's 31 goals this season prove that Middlesbrough have one of the best finishers in England and in Juninho they have arguably the most talented and dynamic midfielder. They are quick on the break and inventive.

Weaknesses: A collective failure to close opponents down, a lack of organisation in midfield and in defence and too much individualism, which paradoxically is also one of their strengths, are Middlesbrough's major weaknesses.

Motivation: Middlesbrough have never won anything in their 121 year history and that is the biggest single factor driving the club towards victory. They also could become the first team in English soccer history to get relegated and win the F.A. Cup in the same season. Only a victory over Chelsea and a place in Europe next year can possibly keep this team together -- although even then it is doubtful if the foriegn stars will still be around when Middlesbrough are in the first division next season.
